prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity, flat website design mockup for SkillSwap, a college peer skill-exchange and time-banking marketplace. This is a screen design, not a poster or photograph of a device. Follow the Superprof-inspired direction: huge approachable bold rounded sans-serif headlines, warm white #FFFCFA background, pale coral #FFF0ED search area, deep coral #C83B46 buttons, near-black #252326 text, spacious layout, rounded cards. Initials avatars only, no people or photos. No monetary prices, testimonials, invented certifications, inflated statistics, hearts/favourites, chat, or video-call controls. Names and descriptions are synthetic illustrative UI content. Real accessible UI must later replace raster text. Render precise readable text and practical controls. Brand text exactly "SkillSwap". Asset: desktop homepage, landscape viewport 1440 by 1050, edge-to-edge browser content with no browser chrome and no labels outside the screen. Navigation: SkillSwap left, "Explore skills", "How it works", "Teach a skill" middle, "Log in" and coral "Join SkillSwap" right. Large centered headline exactly "Learn something new.
Share what you know." Supporting line "Your time is your currency. Find a skill, meet a peer, and learn together." Wide rounded pale-coral search area with white skill input "What do you want to learn?", mode select "Online", and coral "Find a skill" button. Below, understated subject links "Programming", "Music", "Languages", "Design", "Maths". Section headline "Meet your next learning partner" and right link "Explore all skills". Three tasteful cards with generously rounded softly coloured INITIALS panels; first initials AS, name Ananya Shah, Python, "Online · Programming", "No reviews yet"; second RM, Rohan Mehta, Guitar, "In person · Music", "No reviews yet"; third PK, Priya Kapoor, Graphic Design, "Online · Design", "No reviews yet". Each has short realistic description and "View profile" affordance. No fixed price/rate badge. A compact bottom strip "Teach. Earn minutes. Learn." with three numbered steps "Share a skill", "Earn time credits", "Learn from someone new", and truthful registration statement "Start with 120 minutes". Main visual dominance is typography and search, rather than generic dashboard panels.
